summary: Open-source engine that stores incoming content, makes it searchable by keyword and meaning, and alerts you on topics you follow.

heroCommands.command:
git clone https://github.com/The-Vibe-Company/quivr.git && cd quivr
make dev

sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: Quivr is a backend engine for content that keeps arriving, such as news articles, emails, posts and PDFs. It stores every version, makes each document searchable within seconds, and checks new documents against your saved alerts. Your app talks to it over an HTTP API; it has no user interface of its own.
sixtySeconds.problem: Monitoring a stream of documents for topics you care about usually means stitching together storage, search and alerting. Quivr does all three with citations back to the exact passage.
whoFor: Developers building monitoring or news apps
Teams tracking topics across feeds and mailboxes
Builders giving AI agents searchable, citable sources
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it for durable ingestion, hybrid keyword and semantic search, versioned documents, alerts with reasons, and an MCP server for agents.
requirements: Linux x86_64 or a Mac with Apple Silicon
Go (version in go.mod), Python 3.12 with venv, and jq
About 1 GB download on first start

overview: Send documents one by one or in batches, or let Quivr collect them on a schedule from RSS feeds, Microsoft 365 mailboxes and X lists. Plugins read files such as PDFs.

Search by keywords, meaning or both; every result cites its passage, document and version. Save alerts like "harbour strike" AND (ferry OR port) or plain-language descriptions, and read matches or receive signed webhooks. quivr mcp lets agents search and quote it.

Run make dev to start it in Docker, then follow the Quickstart (about fifteen minutes). make demo adds a web app at http://127.0.0.1:5183. Quivr 2's /v0 API stays compatible across 2.x. It is MIT licensed.
limitations: Developer setup needs Docker, Go, Python and jq
